disputed: Zeldin and the administration argue deregulation and economic growth ('energy dominance') can proceed together without net public-health harm, and that many Biden-era rules were themselves excessive; this is a policy dispute, not a settled empirical fact, though independent scientific bodies broadly support the underlying climate science the Endangerment Finding was based on. The long-term health and environmental costs of these specific rollbacks will not be fully measurable for years.

items: Trump reversed more than 125 Biden-era climate policies in his first months back in office, following a similar pattern to over 100 rollbacks during his first term. He signed an executive order in February 2025 creating a National Energy Dominance Council to expand drilling. (DevelopmentAid (https://www.developmentaid.org/news-stream/post/191994/trumps-war-on-climate-policies))

Executive Order 14219 (January 31, 2025) imposed a '10-to-1' deregulation mandate, requiring agencies to identify 10 existing rules to eliminate for every new rule created - a structural incentive to remove protections regardless of their public-health record. (Earth911 (https://earth911.com/business-policy/trump-policy-costs-to-the-environment-and-people/))

On February 12, 2026, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin announced the repeal of the 2009 Endangerment Finding - the legal basis for federal greenhouse-gas regulation of cars, power plants, and oil fields - calling it 'the single largest deregulatory action in the history of the United States.' EPA had already announced in March 2025 it would review 31 major environmental regulations for rollback. (Earth911 (https://earth911.com/business-policy/trump-policy-costs-to-the-environment-and-people/))

The Associated Press reported the EPA froze billions of dollars in previously allocated clean-energy funding and disrupted agency scientific research during 2025. Early actions included delaying a Toxic Substances Control Act rule addressing trichloroethylene, a chemical linked to cancer, liver damage, and Parkinson's disease. (AP, via SEJ/Yahoo (https://www.sej.org/node/51866); Earth911 (https://earth911.com/business-policy/trump-policy-costs-to-the-environment-and-people/))

The EPA's largest employee union president called resulting staff cuts 'devastating,' citing the dismantling of research and development offices and the firing of employees who had signed a dissenting letter. Historian Douglas Brinkley characterized the agency's posture as reverting to a pre-EPA, pre-1970 regulatory environment. (AP, via Castanet (https://www.castanetkamloops.net/news/World/591670/Trumps-EPA-in-2025-A-fossil-fuel-friendly-approach-to-deregulation))

summary: Since January 2025, the Trump administration has pursued what it calls deregulation and 'energy dominance,' rolling back a large body of environmental and public-health rules.
title: Environmental deregulation under EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin
